documents.title: Lease contract
documents.why: The increase can take effect only from the next termination date; the lease records the termination dates (and any graduated-rent or index clause, arts. 269b–269c).

must_show: date from which the increase applies
whether the form approved by the canton is used (for a graduated-rent step, whether it is in writing: art. 269d para. 5)
any threat of termination in it or in the covering letter
for an index-linked increase: the old and new index values
if the landlord gave no notice at all, that absence is itself the finding (art. 269d para. 2 let. a)
documents.title: Landlord's rent increase notice (with any covering letter)
documents.why: An increase is void without the prescribed form or without reasons; only the notice itself shows the form used and the reasons given, and where no notice exists its absence is the point to establish.

must_show: how it was delivered (registered-mail tracking, envelope or acknowledgement)
documents.title: Proof of the date the notice was received
documents.why: The challenge runs 30 days from receiving the notice (German: from its being communicated); proof of the date of receipt is needed to check that period, and it also shows when the notice was given relative to the ten-day rule of art. 269d para. 1.

must_show: share passed on to the rent
documents.title: Landlord's breakdown of the cost increases or additional services, with the supporting invoices, interest notices or cost statements
documents.why: A rent justified by cost increases or additional services is in general not unfair; the underlying invoices, interest notices or cost statements, with the landlord's breakdown, ordinarily show whether the increase is so justified.

documents.title: Landlord's notice of termination
documents.why: The increase is void if accompanied by a notice of termination; the notice shows whether it accompanied the increase.

facts.question: Which tenancy dispute does the claim concern: a defect of the dwelling (mould, damp, heating), a termination of the lease by the landlord, or a rent increase?
Does the claim state that the landlord has announced, demanded or charged a higher rent for the dwelling, by a notice, a letter, an invoice or otherwise (whether or not on an official form)?
Does the claim state that the increase is a step fixed in advance in the lease, by which the rent rises periodically by fixed amounts (graduated rent)?
Does the claim state that the increase applies a clause of the lease linking the rent to an index (such as the Swiss consumer price index)?

Does the increase notice give, as its reason, higher costs for the landlord (for example higher mortgage interest or operating costs) or additional services or works by the landlord (for example a renovation)?
Does the claim state that, together with the rent increase, the landlord gave notice of termination?

notes.text: Convention of this benchmark (not law): A fact that the file does not mention is taken as not alleged, and the rules are applied as if it were absent. Silence never ends a process: where a fact's absence would end it, the unmentioned fact is unresolved. The defining event is never presumed: if the file does not mention it, it is unresolved. A fact that the file raises and leaves unsettled is open. The defining event (increase_applied) and any always-stated fact carry no presumption.
